A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAND study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAND evaluations on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and WebShop, together with component ablations, deliberation analyses and token-cost measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 2–4, Figures 3–4 and Appendix A. The separately attributed comparison results in Appendix B do not affect this assessment.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same initialization, action sampling, execution-guided critique, deliberation synthesis, optional expert switching and iterative finetuning. The inference procedure and appendix prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ALFWorld and ScienceWorld on seen and unseen tasks and WebShop in Appendix A. Newly cited work on GUI agents and document question answering does not add evaluated tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same model rows and SFT, ETO, KnowAgent, WKM and MPO-based comparisons. Appendix B retains Q, QLASS, AgentRM-BoN and AgentRM-Beam; its table is renumbered without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and counts, model backbones, average-reward evaluation, decoding temperatures and training schedules are unchanged. Both versions use five sampled candidate actions for the main experiments, three for WebShop and three SAND iterations.

E4.justification: The SAS/EAC ablations in Table 3, per-step reward and deliberation analysis in Figure 3, difficulty-band analysis in Figure 4 and token-cost study in Table 4 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Figure 4 retains the same distributions of deliberation rates across tasks, without introducing uncertainty estimates across runs.

E6.justification: All matched numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. Table 2 retains iteration-3 averages of 88.9 for Llama-3.1-8B and 84.6 for Qwen2.5-7B. WebShop retains SAND scores of 68.5, 72.4 and 71.8 across iterations despite Table 5 becoming Table 6.

T1.justification: The task formulation and Equations 1–7 retain the same trajectory probabilities, inconsistency indicator and training objectives. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about self-taught action deliberation, approximately 20% improvement over initial SFT and advantages over agent-tuning baselines. Copyediting and added citations do not change their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of generalization gains and selective deliberation, ScienceWorld shortcut caveat, inference-cost limitation and Appendix B qualification about differing comparator backbones are retained. No substantive interpretation or applicability boundary changes.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 retains the same batch size, learning rate, epoch schedule, OpenRLHF implementation and eight A100 80GB GPUs. Appendix C preserves all prompt templates. No implementation disclosure or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight cited works, including the GUI agents survey, Doc-ReAct, DICE and papers or surveys on active learning, reasoning, retrieval and alignment. These supplement existing background passages without substantially changing SAND's positioning or novelty argument.

P1.justification: Scattered copyedits correct wording such as 'alternatives actions' to 'alternative actions', 'world knowledge mode' to 'world knowledge model' and 'AFLWorld' to 'ALFWorld'. The section organization and narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The appendix tables swap numbers: WebShop changes from Table 5 to Table 6, and the PRM/Q-value comparison from Table 6 to Table 5. Appendix material reflows, and Figure 5 moves onto its own page. Main figures and table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds background citations and repairs scattered wording, providing small editorial polish. The method, experimental evidence, interpretations, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, while appendix reflow redistributes existing material. These limited adjustments do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
